summary: Olympic National Park cabin site: 1930s cabin, AWS cabin built 1942, burned about 1972; stove parts and a flat site described, no tower.

facts.design: Small wooden cabin of native materials, no tower; sources give 10 by 20 feet (1942 AWS) and 12 by 20 feet (1954 USGS)
facts.status_note: Cabin burned about 1972; no standing structure is described; remains are stove parts and a flat cabin site

access.note: Inside Olympic National Park; road cleared to the park boundary in 2020 but a washout blocks the most direct driving route; no closure described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: About one mile along the ridge from the park boundary, mostly cross-country through old-growth forest; nothing to climb

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey party first monumented the summit as SPRUCE
AWS built a 10 x 20 foot cabin of native materials after taking up the site; the earlier 1930s cabin is not confirmed in the AWS papers
Photo caption shows AWS observers at Spruce Lookout; station planned for yearlong occupancy
USGS party described the wooden cabin as 12 by 20 feet, 15 feet in height
Burned about 1972; a 1974 USGS visit records it was completely burned by the Park Service
Register photos dated 8/26/2000 show scattered stove parts and pieces of a wood stove
Registered January 10, 2011; nominated by Irene Potter
Road cleared to the park boundary; a washout blocks the most direct driving route

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Firelookout.com describe a 1930s cabin. WillhiteWeb cites a cabin inventory for the 1930s but finds no mention of an earlier cabin in the 1942 AWS papers, which describe a newly built cabin. The 1930s cabin is unconfirmed and both are reported.
AWS papers describe a 10 x 20 foot cabin in 1942; a 1954 USGS party gave 12 by 20 feet. Not resolved; both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Brief agency (National Park Service) confirmed. Construction date disputed: the 1930s cabin is cited secondhand from a cabin inventory; the 1942 AWS cabin is the one described in the AWS papers. Fire-lookout use rests on one WillhiteWeb statement and one photo caption. Remains come from undated photo captions and an undated visit. Access 'public' is a judgement: park land, no closure described. No new photo URLs captured.
